Calculate the uncertainty associated with a tracked cycle based on the frequency uncertainty of the FFT

Source: R/fft_uncertainty.R
fft_uncertainty.Rd

Fourier counterpart of wavelet_uncertainty. A tracked cycle (depth, period) gets an uncertainty in frequency that equals the bin spacing of an FFT of the analysed record (\(1/T\), the practical resolution) or the Heisenberg-Gabor limit (\(1/(4 \pi T)\)), see fft_frequency_uncertainty. In contrast to the wavelet the uncertainty does not depend on the frequency, only on the length of the record (or of the window of an evolutive spectrum). The uncertain frequencies are converted to curves of period (sedimentation rate) and with curve2time to uncertain time models.

Usage

fft_uncertainty(
  tracked_cycle = NULL,
  period_of_tracked_cycle = NULL,
  signal_length = NULL,
  type = c("practical", "gabor"),
  multi = 1,
  verbose = FALSE,
  genplot_time = FALSE,
  genplot_uncertainty = FALSE,
  keep_editable = FALSE
)

Arguments

tracked_cycle

Curve of the tracked cycle, e.g. the output of track_period_wavelet: a matrix or data frame with depth in column 1 and the period of the tracked cycle (in the same depth unit, e.g. metres) in column 2; further columns are ignored. Required (Default=NULL).

period_of_tracked_cycle

Duration of one cycle of the tracked cycle in time (numeric, > 0, e.g. 405 for the 405-kyr eccentricity cycle); passed to curve2time and sets the time unit of the output. Required (Default=NULL).

signal_length

Length of the record (or of the window of an evolutive spectrum) that sets the frequency uncertainty, in the depth unit of tracked_cycle (numeric, > 0). NULL uses the depth range of tracked_cycle. Default=NULL.

type

Definition of the frequency uncertainty (character): "practical" uses the FFT bin spacing \(1/T\); "gabor" uses the Heisenberg-Gabor limit \(1/(4 \pi T)\), which is about 12.6 times smaller. Default=c("practical", "gabor"), i.e. "practical".

multi

Multiple of the frequency uncertainty that is added to and subtracted from the frequency of the tracked cycle (numeric, > 0; e.g. 2 for twice the uncertainty). Default=1.

verbose

Print the total duration, its uncertainty and the frequency uncertainty (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

genplot_time

Plot the time-depth curves of the mean, lower and upper uncertainty (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

genplot_uncertainty

Plot the period-depth curves of the tracked cycle with its lower and upper uncertainty (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

keep_editable

Keep the graphical parameters (par) of the plot after the function returns, so that features can be added to it (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE restores the previous settings. Default=FALSE.

Value

A data frame with the columns "depth", "period", "frequency", "uncertainty in frequency", "uncertainty in frequency x_times", "time mean", "time plus x_times" and "time min x_times" (the same layout as wavelet_uncertainty, with the Fourier uncertainty), and the attribute "type".

Examples

tr <- data.frame(depth = seq(0, 100, by = 1), period = 10 + 0 * seq(0, 100, by = 1))
unc <- fft_uncertainty(tr, period_of_tracked_cycle = 100, type = "practical")
tail(unc, 2)
#>     depth period frequency uncertainty in frequency
#> 100    99     10       0.1                     0.01
#> 101   100     10       0.1                     0.01
#>     uncertainty in frequency x_times time mean time min x_times
#> 100                             0.01       990              891
#> 101                             0.01      1000              900
#>     time plus x_times
#> 100              1089
#> 101              1100
